Heard Sri Shivanand V. Pattanshetti, learned counsel for the appellant-accused and Sri Veeranagouda Malipatil, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

2. Appellant has been convicted in S.C. No.95/2019 on 21.11.2020 by the I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Vijayapura, (for short 'Trial Court'), for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 307 of IPC and sentenced as under:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR "Acting U/Sec. 235(2) Cr.P.C accused is convicted and sentenced undergo simple imprisonment for one year for the offence punishable U/Sec. 498-A IPC and shall pay fine of Rs.2,000/-(Two thousand only).

3.

Facts in brief, which are utmost necessary for disposal of the present appeal, are as under:
3.1
The charge-sheet material would reveal that PW1-Jayashree is wife of the appellant and their marriage took place and they were living happily for sometime and a son by name Preetham was born to them.

3.2 It is contended that thereafter accused addicted to liquor and was not lookingafter the PW1 and her son and under the influence of liquor he used to picked up NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR quarrel with the PW1 practically and used to physically and mentally harass her.
It was also alleged that he never came to contribute for the household expenses and by doing coolie work the PW1 was maintaining the family.
3.3 When the matter stood thus, it is alleged that in the intervening night of 25.05.2019 to 26.05.2019, PW1 was sleeping.
At that time accused with an intention to murder his wife, with the help of pillow (M.O.1) tried to smoother her and also pressed her neck.
When the said attempt was resisted by PW1, her leg touched the vessels and it fell down and on hearing the sound the vessels, her son Preetham came and opened the door.
At that juncture, she told her son that appellant tried to murder her.
Immediately, he raised alarm and neighbours came and on seeing them, the appellant ran away from the spot.
3.4 Immediately, she was taken to the hospital by the mother of the PW1 and others.
In the hospital, she has been examined.

PW5 is the Doctor, who examined NC:
2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR PW1, issued Wound Certificate as per Ex.P5, wherein, no fracture was seen either in the spine or on the shoulder or in nasal bone nor any Parashuram S/O Goolappa Hirekurubar vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94326144/

sentences.text: Based on the complaint, the police investigated the matter and filed charge-sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 307 of IPC.
Accused was arrested and later on enlarged on bail.
5. Thereafter, charges were framed for the aforesaid offences and accused having pleaded not guilty, trial was held.

6. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined six witnesses, comprising of complainant as PW1 and a circumstantial witness who heard loud hue and cry and reached the house of the complainant by name Mudkappa as PW2, Neelavva, Balappa as the circumstantial witnesses, the Doctor as PW5 and the Investigating Officer as PW6.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR 7.
Prosecution placed on record six documents, which were exhibited and marked as Exs.P1 to P6 comprising of Complaint, Mahazar, Photographs, Wound Certificate and FIR.

8. The pillow, which was allegedly used in the incident was seized under Ex.P2 was marked as MO.2.
9.
After conclusion of recording of evidence, the learned Trial Judge recorded accused statement as is contemplated under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., wherein, accused has denied the incriminating material.
But he did not offer any written submissions, though he has admitted to examine witnesses on his behalf, he did not examine any witnesses.

10. Thereafter, learned Trial Judge heard the arguments of the parties and on cumulative consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record, convicted the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 307 of IPC and sentenced as referred to supra.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR 11.

Being aggrieved by the same, appellant is before this Court in this appeal on the following grounds:
That, the judgment of conviction & order of sentence passed by the learned judge is contrary to the facts of the case, evidence on record & against the settled principles of law.
That, the learned Sessions Judge has committed a serious error in convicting the appellant without properly appreciating the evidence in its right prospective manner.

sentences.text: That, looking in to Ex.P-1 complaint the alleged incident was occurred on 25-05-2019 at about 12:30 a.m.
However complaint was given on the very same day that on 25-05- 2019 at about 9:15 Hrs.
So, prior to the alleged incident as mentioned in the complaint, the police have registered the case after receiving the typed complaint.
Hence, this fact itself clarifies the fact that it is a case of false implication.

That, looking in to the evidence of PW- 1/complainant, in the cross examination the complainant stated that as per the instance of NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR police she has given complaint and subsequently denied the same and further stated that as per her say only police have written the complaint, but looking in to the Ex.P-1 it is a typed complaint.
So, trial court without appreciating this fact straight away convicted the appellant.
Hence, the approach of the trial court is highly erroneous and illegal and same is liable to be set aside.

That, looking in to the cross examination PW- 1 at the time of alleged incident while making effort to rescue from the act of accused some utensils fell down, because of sound her son one Preetam wake up and made hue and cry and call the people, but prosecution is not made effort to led the evidence of said Preetam.
So, it creates the doubt regarding the veracity of the prosecution case.
Hence, judgment of conviction order of sentence is liable to be set aside.

That, as per the prosecution appellant in the night hours pressed the face with the help of pillow forcibly and try to commit her murder by smothering, but as per the evidence Doctor i.e. PW-5 said that, the said injuries can be caused when contact with hard and - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR blunt object.
So, the story narrated by the prosecution unnatural and unbelievable one.
That, looking in to the evidence collected by the prosecution absolutely there is no material to attract the provisions of Sec 498(A) of IPC.

To attract the provisions of Sec 498(A)
of IPC there should be some positive evidence with regard to any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life,
limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman or harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
Hence, trial Court ought to have acquitted the appellant on the ground of lack of evidence in proving the provisions of Sec 498(A) of IPC.

That, looking in to the evidence of PW-1, 2, 3 & 4 absolutely there is no material with regard to cruelty or ill-treatment and intention on the part of the appellant to - 11 - Parashuram S/O Goolappa Hirekurubar vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94326144/
5 NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR commit the alleged offences.

sentences.text: So, absolutely there is no material to attract the provisions of sec. 498 (A) & 307 of IPC.

That, the whole case of the prosecution is depends upon the here say witnesses and highly interested witnesses to convict the appellant, under this circumstances trial court ought to have taken more care to evaluate the evidence on record and acquitted the appellant.
That, there is a lot of inconsistence of evidence regarding filing of complaint and the manner in which investigation is conducted.
This fact is not been properly appreciated by the trial court.
That, great care must be taken in evaluating evidence and if the evidence relied on is reasonably capable of two inferences, the one in favour of the accused must be accepted.
But this principle is not been properly appreciated by the trial court.

That, there is no legal evidence collected by the prosecution during investigation as well - 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR as during the trial, even then trial court convicted the appellant is bad-in-law.
That, without admitting the case of the prosecution, the sentence imposed by the trial court too higher side.
That, trial court failed to put the questions regarding the incrementing materials & circumstances against the accused while recording the 313 statement.
That, court below ought to have disbelieved the say of witnesses who are very much interested in convicting the appellant.
That, it is respectfully submitted that, the learned Sessions Judge has not at all appreciated the case of the appellant in the light to human probabilities and the same has vitiated the findings.
The reason assigned by court in convicting the appellant is illegal and incorrect.
The same has resulted in miscarriage of justice to the appellant.

12. Sri Shivanand Pattanshetti, learned counsel for the appellant reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal - 13 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR memorandum, contended that the prosecution case is nothing but a story woven, only with an intention to some how put the appellant behind the bars and the learned Trial Court has not properly appreciated the material evidence on record resulting in miscarriage of justice and sought for allowing the appeal.
13.

He would point out that alleged eyewitness to the incident, in terms of Section 6 of the Evidence Act, namely Preetham, who is the son of the appellant and the PW1, being not examined by the prosecution, exposes the hollowness in the case of the prosecution and sought for allowing the appeal.

sentences.text: Alternatively, Sri Shivanand Pattanshetti, would contend that in the absence of any fracture of nasal bone, theory of smoothening cannot be countenanced in law; at best, the material on record would support only an offence under Section 498A of IPC.
Therefore, the custody period already undergone by the appellant may be treated as a period of imprisonment and sought for allowing the appeal to that extent.
16. Per contra, Sri Veeranagouda Malipatil, learned High Court Government Pleader supports the impugned judgment.

17. He would further contend that the fact of the lodging complaint immediately after the incident and examination of the victim PW1 in the Government Hospital on the same day by the Doctor who examined the PW1 and issued Wound Certificate vide Ex.P5 shows that the incident as is propounded by the prosecution did occur, which has been rightly appreciated by the learned Trial Judge and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
18.

He would further point out that mere absence of fracture of nasal bone would not be sufficient enough to disbelieve the theory of the prosecution that there was an - 15 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR attempt to take away the life of PW1 by smoothening and thus,
sought for dismissal of the appeal.
19. Having heard the arguments of both sides, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

20. On such perusal of the material on record, the following points would arise for consideration in this appeal:
1) Whether the material evidence placed on record by the prosecution would be sufficient enough to maintain the order of conviction of the appellant for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 307 of IPC?

2) Whether the impugned judgment is suffering from any legal infirmity or perversity and thus calls for interference by this Court?
3) Whether the sentence is excessive?
 4) What order?

sentences.text: Regarding point Nos.1 and 2:-
21 In the case on hand, the relationship of the appellant with the PW1 and the son by name Preetham is born in the wedlock is not in dispute.

22. It is also found from the material evidence placed on record that the relationship between the appellant and the PW1 was not cordial inasmuch as appellant used to consume liquor and used to harass the PW1 everyday by not only abusing her, but also assaulting her.
Material evidence also discloses that the appellant was not contributing any money for the household expenses and used to abuse the PW1 physically and mentally.
23. These aspects of the matter are sufficient enough to maintain conviction of the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
Except denying the incriminating circumstances though accused has agreed to examine evidence, but he failed to do so.

25. Insofar as charge under Section 307 of IPC is concerned, it is the specific case of the prosecution that with the aid of M.O.1 - pillow, accused on the intervening night between 25.05.2019 and 26.05.2019 at about 12.30 a.m., tried to smoother the PW1 and in order to take away the life of the PW1.
It is found from the records that PW1 raised alarm and resisted the attempt of the accused, her leg touched vessels and it fell down.

Soon after hearing the sound of vessels falling down, son of the appellant and the PW1 namely, Preetham came there and he saw the incident and reported the same to the others and whereby the neighbours and mother came to the house of the appellant and rescued the PW1 and on seeing them, appellant ray away from the spot.
To establish the same, the prosecution failed to examine the son of the PW1 as a witness.

- 18 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR Parashuram S/O Goolappa Hirekurubar vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94326144/
8 26.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, according to the version of the PW1, two more eyewitnesses to the incident namely Siddamma Hiremath and Shantabai Dange, who pacified the quarrel and rescued the PW1.
27. Pertinently neither Siddamma Hiremath nor Shantabai Dange have been cited as witnesses by the prosecution and examine them to support the case of the prosecution.

28. Taking note of all these aspects of the matter and also taking note of the size of M.O.1, as is seen in photographs, which is said to have been seized under Ex.P2 Mahazar, theory that is put forward by the prosecution that with the help of M.O.1 appellant tried to smoother the PW1 cannot be countenanced in law.
29. Further, there is no fracture of the nasal bone and PW1 herself stated and M.O.1 was used to smoother the mouth and not the nose.
Further, there is no fracture - 19 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR on the shoulder bone or the collar bone or no fracture in the spine.

30. Taking note all these aspects, this Court is of the considered opinion that the material evidence is not sufficient enough to maintain the conviction of the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC.
31.

In the absence of any blood injury, the alleged acts of the appellant should be scaled down from the offence under Section 307 of IPC to 323 of IPC.
32.
Accordingly, in view of the foregoing discussions, point Nos.1 and 2 are answered partly in the affirmative.

Regarding point No.3:-
33.

In view of the foregoing discussion, when this Court scaled down the offence from 307 of IPC to 323 of - 20 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR IPC, and maintaining conviction of the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC, the custody period already undergone by the appellant, if treated as period of imprisonment by enhancing the fine amount in a sum Rs.50,000/-, of which a sum of Rs.45,000/- can be paid as compensation to PW1, ends of justice would be met in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.
34.
Accordingly, point No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.

Regarding point No.4:-

sentences.text:
In view of the finding of this Court regarding point Nos.1 to 3 as above, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) While maintaining the conviction of the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC, appellant/accused is - 21 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:3813 HC-KAR acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC,
instead he has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 323 of IPC.

iii) Custody period already undergone by the appellant-accused would be treated as period of imprisonment for the proved offences under Sections 498A and 323 of IPC by directing the appellant to pay enhanced fine of Rs.50,000/-.

iv) Appellant is granted to pay the enhanced fine amount till 31.08.2025, failure to pay the fine,
within 31.08.2025, appellant shall undergo imprisonment for a period of two years.
v) Out of the fine amount recovered, Rs.45,000/- is ordered to be paid as compensation to the PW1 under due identification.
